topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the accumulation of cellular changes as the basis of stepwise cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why cancer must be understood in the context of organised tissues rather than isolated tumour cells.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumours through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how invasion and spread distinguish malignant tumours from contained benign growth, using anatomical and histological examples.

topics.label: Tumour progression and the clinical risks of benign growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the transition from benign growth to malignancy and explain why remaining benign does not necessarily make a tumour harmless.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and how metastatic disease can lead to fatal organ failure.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Cancer presentation and screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the need for early cancer detection and assess how effectively screening can meet that need in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students towards revision and forthcoming teaching.
